title: Audit, price safely and lead: UX as a professional service

say: Audit, price safely and lead: UX as a professional service.
This is the video for module three of UX Design Fundamentals: consulting, leadership and a senior portfolio.
A UX audit is a focused review that finds the usability problems costing a business most, and recommends fixes in order. It is clearly scoped, fast to deliver, and often leads to redesign work.

say: Interview the founder, the product manager, a developer and customer support, for 30 to 45 minutes each.
First ask: if this audit succeeds, which number moves?

panel.heading: Ask before you touch the product
items: Known pain: top five support tickets

say: Ask who the users are, on what devices and networks. Ask what analytics, reviews and support logs exist, and request viewer access.

panel.heading: Ask before you touch the product
items: Known pain: top five support tickets

say: Ask support for the top five complaint types. Then note budget, deadline and legal limits, and who approves your recommendations.

panel.heading: Ask before you touch the product
items: Known pain: top five support tickets

say: Pick three to five critical tasks and walk through them on a mid-range Android phone on a normal network. Rate each problem on Nielsen's scale from 0 to 4.
For example, Chiamaka audits an Abuja fashion store checkout. The Continue and Back buttons look identical, causing occasional mis-taps. Severity 2.
The phone field rejects numbers typed with spaces, and the error just says Invalid input. Frequent and confusing. Severity 3.
The delivery fee appears only on the final payment screen. Every buyer meets it, and it causes abandonment. Severity 4.
The owner fixed the top two within a week, because the evidence was clear and the fixes were cheap.

panel.heading: Rate every problem from 0 to 4
panel.rule: Rate by frequency, impact and persistence.

say: Under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, recordings, names, phone numbers and opinions are personal data. Use a plain-language consent form that says what is recorded, why, and for how long.

panel.heading: Research data and the law
items: Label people P1, P2; names kept separately
Blur faces, phone numbers, account details
Store securely; delete on the contract date

say: Do not start work without the agreed deposit. Be wary of clients who overpay and ask you to refund the difference, or send payment links asking for your card PIN or OTP.
Always verify transfers in your own banking app, not from a screenshot.

panel.heading: Protect yourself from payment scams
items: No work before the agreed deposit
Beware clients who overpay and want refunds
Never give your card PIN or OTP
Verify transfers in your own banking app

say: A critique reviews work in progress against its goals. It is not a vote on taste. The presenter states the goal and the feedback wanted.

panel.heading: Three roles in a design critique

cards.d: States the goal and the feedback they need.
Keeps time and steers comments back to the goal.
Given the goal of X, I noticed Y, which might cause Z.

say: To remember. Start every audit with an agreed outcome, and rate problems 0 to 4 with evidence. Base your day rate on your goal plus costs, divided by billable days.
Treat recordings as personal data. And in your portfolio, show decisions, trade-offs and measured results.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Start every audit with an agreed outcome
Day rate: goal plus costs, over billable days
Senior case studies show decisions and results
